The organization works with lawmakers, including veterans and elected officials representing frontline communities, through leadership councils and specialized task forces. Fellows may therefore gain exposure to activities involving: Policy research Legislative advocacy Public policy communication Stakeholder engagement Political outreach Environmental policy Climate policy Energy security Clean transportation Climate finance Land and water conservation Nature-based solutions International policy initiatives The organization emphasizes peer-to-peer education , based on the idea that elected officials can be particularly effective in educating and influencing fellow lawmakers. EOPA states that its policy work has included initiatives ranging from international energy-security proposals and United Nations climate negotiations to national and state-level environmental policies. 2. Education and Training The second major area is education and professional development. EOPA works jointly with the University of San Francisco to operate a Public Leadership Certificate designed to strengthen the leadership and policy capabilities of lawmakers and civic leaders. The program covers areas including: Emotional intelligence Leadership Management Public speaking Body language Value-based communications Legislative procedures Cybersecurity Empathy Fundraising Participants also have opportunities to interact with elected officials who have played significant roles in public policy. The fellowship provides an opportunity for fellows to potentially participate in this leadership certificate program. EOPA states that more than 200 leaders from around the world apply for the Public Leadership Certificate, with approximately 37 participants accepted on average . This makes access to the certificate a potentially significant professional-development benefit for successful fellows. 3. Media and Storytelling EOPA also places significant emphasis on communication, journalism, storytelling, and visual media. The organization has an in-house film production arm that develops media intended to educate lawmakers, journalists, and members of the public. Its work has included: Digital advertisements Short documentaries Environmental campaigns Water-security storytelling Policy communication Video production Print articles Letters Op-eds Policy solutions The organization also operates ProtectEarth.News , a newsmagazine intended to bring together videos, articles, policy solutions, letters, and opinion pieces. For fellows interested in strategic communications, journalism, public relations, digital media, filmmaking, storytelling, advocacy communications, or political communication , this area could provide particularly relevant experience. Who Is the Fellowship Looking For? The Solon Fellowship is intended for motivated and dedicated young professionals who are prepared to support and potentially lead different types of organizational projects and programs. The opportunity specifically highlights candidates interested in areas such as: Research Partnerships Fundraising Video editing Video production Op-ed writing Data management Project management Policy-related work Communications Public leadership Environmental advocacy Applicants do not necessarily need to specialize in only one of these areas. The fellowship appears particularly suitable for people who are adaptable and interested in working across different functions within a mission-driven organization. Fellowship Responsibilities and Potential Areas of Contribution Because EOPA works across policy, communications, education, and mobilization, fellows may have opportunities to contribute to different projects depending on their skills and the organization s needs. Potential areas include: Research and policy Fellows may contribute to research activities supporting environmental and public policy initiatives. This could include gathering information, analyzing policy issues, preparing briefing materials, supporting advocacy initiatives, or contributing to written policy products. Partnerships Fellows interested in stakeholder engagement may contribute to partnership development and relationship-building activities. This could involve working with elected officials, organizations, civic leaders, environmental groups, and other stakeholders. Fundraising The program also exposes fellows to nonprofit and political fundraising. This includes learning how fundraising messages can be developed around shared values and how organizations can build stronger relationships with potential funders. Communications Fellows may support communications activities such as: Writing Editing Story development Public messaging Campaign communication Media materials Value-based communications Video production Candidates with media-production skills may have opportunities to contribute to video editing and production. Op-ed writing The organization s emphasis on policy communication creates opportunities for fellows interested in opinion writing, public commentary, and policy storytelling. Data and project management Candidates with analytical and organizational skills can potentially contribute to data-management and project-management activities. Fellowship Duration and Working Hours The fellowship is structured as a four-month program . Fellows can work between: 20 and 40 hours per week This flexible structure can make the program suitable for individuals who need to balance professional development with other academic, professional, or personal commitments. The organization also indicates that the fellowship may be extended beyond the initial four-month period . Remote and International Work Options One of the notable features of the Solon Fellowship is its flexible location arrangement. The fellowship can be undertaken: Online/remotely At EOPA s office in Rockland, Maine At its Washington, DC location Internationally The availability of international participation is particularly important for applicants who are not based in the United States. However, applicants should carefully review the application form and any subsequent communication from EOPA to confirm whether particular positions have location-specific requirements. Emotional Intelligence and Public Leadership Training The emotional intelligence component focuses on improving participants ability to: Understand other people s perspectives Empathize with others Listen accurately Communicate authentically Work effectively with teams Improve team performance Encourage creativity Develop stronger leadership practices These skills can be particularly valuable for professionals working in public administration, government, nonprofit organizations, advocacy, development, communications, and community engagement. This makes the training potentially valuable for people pursuing careers in strategic communication, public relations, political communication, environmental advocacy, development communication, or journalism. The training explores how organizations can build relationships with funders by connecting fundraising appeals to shared values and demonstrating empathy. Participation can therefore provide fellows with an additional professional-development experience beyond their day-to-day fellowship responsibilities. For early-career professionals, this network can potentially support future collaborations, employment opportunities, policy initiatives, and professional development. The CV and portfolio materials should therefore be prepared in one of the accepted languages where required. These countries are: South Africa Benin Cameroon Ghana Guinea Kenya Mali Mozambique Uganda Republic of the Congo Rwanda Senegal Applicants must reside in one of these countries to be eligible for the Relay Scheme. Applicants living in other African countries should not assume that they are eligible simply because the programme is generally focused on Sub-Saharan Africa. The Relay Scheme specifically identifies these 12 participating countries. What Will Participants Do? Participants will work directly with a Creative Tandem project in their own country . The practical component allows participants to apply their communications skills to real cultural projects rather than learning only through theoretical training. Depending on the project and participant s role, activities may involve areas such as: Storytelling Participants can use storytelling techniques to communicate the ideas, people, activities, and impact associated with cultural projects. Effective storytelling can help audiences understand why a cultural project matters and encourage greater engagement. Social Media Participants will develop experience communicating cultural projects through social media. This can include developing content, engaging audiences, supporting campaigns, and using appropriate platforms to increase visibility. Editorial Planning Editorial strategy is another important component of the programme. Participants can develop skills in planning content, identifying relevant themes, structuring communications activities, and maintaining consistent messaging. Media Relations Participants can gain practical exposure to communicating with media outlets and journalists. This can include developing media-facing content and supporting efforts to generate media attention for cultural projects. Cultural Reporting The programme also provides an opportunity to develop experience in cultural reporting and communications. This can involve communicating stories related to performing arts, music, cultural activities, creative practitioners, and related projects. Training Programme The professional development component includes 10 themed training sessions . The official programme identifies areas including: Storytelling Social media Editorial strategy Press relations The sessions are designed to strengthen participants practical communications capabilities while they work on their assigned cultural projects. The training component allows participants to complement their existing professional experience with structured learning. Individual Mentoring Participants will also receive one-to-one mentoring . Individual mentoring can provide a more personalized professional development experience, allowing participants to receive guidance relevant to their own career development and communications work. Combined with the group training sessions and practical project experience, the mentoring component creates a multi-dimensional professional development structure. Professional Network Another important benefit of the programme is access to a professional network. Participants will have opportunities to connect with communications professionals from the participating African countries as well as the broader Connect Create ecosystem. This can help participants: Exchange ideas. Learn from professionals in other countries. Discover different approaches to cultural communications. Build professional relationships. Explore potential future collaborations. Gain exposure to regional cultural and creative networks. For early-career communications professionals, these connections can become an important part of long-term professional development. Training Certificate Participants will receive a training certificate as part of the programme. A certificate can provide formal documentation of participation in the professional development programme and can be included in future professional portfolios, CVs, and applications where appropriate. Financial Support The programme provides an allowance for communication activities carried out for the supported project . The information provided does not specify a single fixed amount for the allowance. Applicants should therefore consult the official guidelines for the precise financial arrangements, eligible activities, and any applicable conditions. Programme Duration The Relay Scheme provides approximately 11 months of support . According to the official timeline, the programme is expected to begin in late January or early February 2027 . This extended period allows participants to combine practical project work with training, mentoring, and professional networking. Application Timeline Applicants should pay close attention to the programme timeline. Applications Open 15 September 2026 Application Deadline 13 October 2026 Shortlisting 14 October to 3 November 2026 During this period, applications will be reviewed and candidates will be shortlisted. Creative Tandem Project Proposal 5 to 19 November 2026 Shortlisted candidates will be asked to submit a proposal for a Creative Tandem project. Announcement of the 16 Connect Create Hubs 7 December 2026 The selected hubs will be announced. Programme Start Late January or early February 2027 The professional development programme is expected to begin around this period. Application Requirements Applicants are required to submit an online application. The application should include: 1. Online Application Form Applicants must complete the designated online application form. 2. Short CV Applicants must provide a short CV in either English or French . The CV should clearly demonstrate relevant professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation. 3. Portfolio Applicants must provide a portfolio containing two to three examples of previous work . The portfolio is important because it allows applicants to demonstrate their practical communications capabilities rather than relying solely on descriptions in their CV. Examples could include relevant work such as: Published articles Journalism work Social media campaigns Digital content Cultural reporting Video or multimedia content Editorial projects Communications campaigns Media work Other professional communications outputs Applicants should choose examples that best demonstrate their communication skills and experience. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should approach the application as an opportunity to demonstrate both professional experience and a clear interest in cultural communications. Demonstrate Relevant Experience Clearly explain your professional experience over the last two to five years. Focus on work that demonstrates communications, journalism, media, content creation, storytelling, or audience engagement. Make Your Portfolio Relevant Do not simply submit random examples of previous work. Choose two or three pieces that demonstrate your strongest and most relevant communications abilities. Where possible, select work that demonstrates: Storytelling Audience engagement Editorial judgment Social media communication Cultural or community reporting Media relations Creative content production Demonstrate Local Understanding Because the programme emphasizes local roots and working with Creative Tandem projects in participants countries, applicants should demonstrate their understanding of their local audience and cultural environment. Explain Your Motivation Applicants should clearly communicate why they are interested in cultural communications and how participation in the programme could contribute to their professional development. Highlight Audience Reach If you have an established audience through social media, media platforms, websites, community networks, or other channels, provide relevant evidence. Audience reach should be presented accurately and, where possible, supported with measurable information. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be particularly relevant to professionals who want to combine communications with culture and the creative industries. Potential applicants include: Early-career journalists Digital communications professionals Social media professionals Content creators Cultural journalists Media presenters Influencers Storytellers Communications specialists Creative-sector communicators The strongest fit will generally be professionals who can demonstrate relevant experience, an active audience, local connections, and a genuine interest in performing arts, music, and cultural industries. About Connect Create The Relay Scheme forms part of the broader Connect Create – Strengthening Cultural Ties Between Africa and Europe programme. Connect Create is the Sub-Saharan Africa component of the Africa–Europe Partnerships for Culture programme, which is funded by the European Union. The wider initiative aims to strengthen cultural ties between Sub-Saharan Africa and the European Union through cooperation, inclusion, sustainability, professional development, and cultural exchange. The programme includes several support areas for professionals in performing arts and music, including: Connect Create Relay Scheme Mentoring Scheme Circulation of Performing Arts and Music Professional Mobility Creative Tandems The Relay Scheme specifically focuses on communications professionals. Focus on Young Professionals Connect Create places particular emphasis on younger generations and emerging cultural scenes. The wider programme recognizes the importance of young people s creativity, energy, and leadership in shaping future Africa–Europe cultural relationships. title: InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ Turn Your Green Idea Into a Viable, Market-Ready Solution
summary: Do you have an innovative idea that could help businesses, communities, or cities become more sustainable, resource-efficient, and environmentally responsible? The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is designed to help promising green and circular-economy ideas move from early concepts to practical, viable, and market-ready solutions. The program supports university students, young innovators, researchers, startups, entrepreneurs, and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the West Bank, including Jerusalem , who are working on solutions related to the green and circular economy. Through a combination of hackathons, specialized mentoring, technical assistance, incubation, networking, and seed funding , participants can receive practical support to develop, test, refine, and implement their ideas. The program provides financial support averaging approximately €8,000 per selected team , together with technical assistance, mentoring, guidance, and incubation support for up to six months. Applications for the InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program are scheduled to open in September 2026 . What Is InnoTadweer: EcoHack+? InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ is an innovation and entrepreneurship support program focused on developing solutions that contribute to a greener and more circular economy in the West Bank. The program is intended for people and organizations with ideas, prototypes, businesses, or existing facilities that could benefit from adopting more sustainable practices. Rather than focusing only on generating ideas, EcoHack+ aims to help participants move through the development process toward practical implementation and market readiness. The program combines several forms of support, including: Hackathons Technical assistance Specialized mentoring Expert guidance Incubation Networking Multidisciplinary team formation Seed funding Support for testing and refining solutions Assistance in moving ideas toward implementation and market readiness This combination allows participants to address both the technical and business aspects of green innovation. The Green and Circular Economy Focus The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program focuses on innovations that can improve the way resources are produced, consumed, reused, recovered, and managed. The green and circular economy approach seeks to reduce waste and resource consumption while creating sustainable economic opportunities. The program welcomes ideas and solutions related to areas such as: Resource Efficiency Solutions that help businesses, organizations, communities, or other users make more efficient use of resources can be considered. This may include innovations that reduce unnecessary consumption of materials, water, energy, or other resources. Waste Valorization EcoHack+ is interested in approaches that transform waste into economic value. Instead of treating waste solely as something to dispose of, participants can explore ways to recover, reuse, process, or convert waste into useful materials, products, or other forms of value. Circular Business Models Participants can develop business models based on circular economy principles. These may involve approaches that extend product lifecycles, encourage reuse, improve recycling, recover valuable materials, reduce waste, or create alternative approaches to resource consumption. Renewable Energy The program also welcomes innovative solutions related to renewable energy and the transition toward more sustainable energy systems. Sustainable Production Ideas that help businesses produce goods or services more sustainably can also fit within the program s focus. This can include approaches designed to reduce resource use, minimize waste, improve production efficiency, or incorporate environmentally responsible processes. Green Technologies EcoHack+ welcomes technological solutions that address environmental and sustainability challenges. Green technologies can potentially be applied across different industries and sectors, depending on the specific challenge being addressed. Sustainable Agriculture The program also includes solutions related to sustainable agriculture and resource-efficient agricultural practices. Participants can explore innovative approaches that contribute to more sustainable agricultural production and resource management. Other Green and Circular Economy Challenges The program is not limited to the examples listed above. It also welcomes other innovative approaches addressing challenges connected to the green and circular economy. Who Can Participate? InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ is designed for a broad range of innovators and organizations. Potential participants include: University students Young innovators Researchers Entrepreneurs Early-stage startups Informal teams Existing micro enterprises Small enterprises Medium enterprises The program therefore accommodates participants at different stages of development, from individuals who have only an initial idea to businesses and organizations that already have an operating facility and want to introduce more sustainable practices. Individual and Team Applications Participants do not necessarily need to have an established team before applying. Applications can be submitted: Individually As part of an existing team For participants who apply individually, the program provides opportunities to connect with people from different disciplines, professional backgrounds, and areas of expertise. This is particularly important because many environmental and circular-economy challenges require collaboration between people with different technical, business, scientific, entrepreneurial, and practical skills. During the hackathon component, participants can receive support in developing multidisciplinary teams. Track A: Idea Development One of the program s tracks is Track A – Idea Development . This track is intended for participants who have an idea but may not yet know how to develop it into a practical solution. It is particularly relevant to: University students Young innovators Entrepreneurs Informal teams Individuals with early-stage ideas The track focuses on early-stage idea development, particularly in the areas of: Resource efficiency Sustainable production Green innovation Circular economy solutions Participants in this stage can use the program s support to develop their initial concept and begin determining how it could become a viable solution. From Idea to Market-Ready Solution A major objective of EcoHack+ is to help participants progress through the different stages of innovation. An idea may initially exist only as a concept. Through the program, participants can receive support to develop and refine that concept. The development process can involve: 1. Identifying the Problem Participants begin by understanding the environmental, resource-efficiency, or circular-economy problem they are attempting to solve. A clearly defined problem can provide the foundation for developing a practical solution. 2. Developing the Idea Participants can work on transforming an initial idea into a more clearly defined innovation or project. This may involve identifying the target users, defining the proposed solution, and determining how the solution could address the identified challenge. 3. Building or Refining a Prototype For participants who already have a prototype, the program can provide support to further develop and refine it. The objective is to move beyond an initial concept toward something that can be tested and evaluated. 4. Mentoring and Technical Assistance Participants receive access to technical assistance, specialized mentoring, and guidance. Expert support can help participants identify challenges, improve their solutions, and consider technical and business requirements. 5. Incubation Selected participants can receive incubation support for up to six months . This provides additional time and support for developing the idea, project, or business. 6. Financial Support Selected teams can receive financial support averaging approximately €8,000 . The funding can provide resources needed to advance a promising solution toward implementation and market readiness, subject to the program s funding requirements and selection procedures. Expected Benefits of the Program Participants selected for InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ can benefit from several forms of support. Financial Support Selected teams are expected to receive financial support averaging around €8,000 . The funding component can help selected teams move their ideas forward and support the development of green or circular-economy solutions. Technical Assistance Participants can receive dedicated technical assistance relevant to developing and improving their solutions. Specialized Mentoring Expert mentors can provide guidance as participants develop their ideas, prototypes, projects, or businesses. Incubation Support Selected participants can receive incubation support for up to six months. Networking Opportunities Participants can connect with people from different professional and academic backgrounds. This can help individuals find collaborators and build multidisciplinary teams. Market Readiness The program aims to help promising ideas progress toward implementation and market readiness. This is particularly important for participants who want to transform an environmental concept into a practical product, service, business model, or project. Who Might Benefit From Applying? The program can be relevant to individuals and organizations at different stages. For example, a university student with an early idea related to waste management could use the program to develop the concept further. A young entrepreneur could use the program to refine a circular business model. A researcher could explore how research findings can be translated into a practical green innovation. An early-stage startup could receive mentoring and funding to improve an existing prototype. An existing MSME could explore how to introduce more resource-efficient or sustainable practices into its operations. The program s broad structure allows different types of applicants to approach green innovation from different starting points. Program Duration The stated duration of the InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is: 18 months Within this broader program period, participants can engage with different activities and forms of support depending on their track and stage of development. Application Period The application period is scheduled to open in: September 2026 The information provided does not specify a final application deadline. Applicants should therefore monitor the official InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ application information for the opening announcement, submission deadline, application requirements, and any updates to the program schedule. Program Geographic Focus The program is implemented in the West Bank, including Jerusalem . Its focus is therefore on supporting green innovation, entrepreneurship, resource efficiency, and circular-economy development within the Palestinian context. Applicants should review the official program eligibility requirements before applying to confirm their geographic eligibility. Supporting Organizations The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is implemented within the Green West Bank and SAWA 2 projects. The program is supported by: The European Union The Belgian Government through DGD Implementation is led by the Belgian Agency for International Cooperation (ENAPEL) in partnership with the Business Center for Innovation, Technology and Entrepreneurship (BCite) at Al-Quds University . The collaboration brings together international development support and local innovation and entrepreneurship expertise. Contribution to the Palestinian Green Economy The program is part of broader efforts to support a greener and more circular Palestinian economy. Through support for green innovation and entrepreneurship, the program seeks to contribute to: Green innovation Entrepreneurship Business competitiveness Resource efficiency Sustainable production Circular economy development Environmental solutions Market-oriented innovation Supporting innovative businesses and young people can also contribute to the development of new products, services, business models, and technologies addressing environmental challenges. Why Multidisciplinary Collaboration Matters Many sustainability challenges cannot be solved through one area of expertise alone. For example, developing a solution for waste valorization may require technical knowledge, environmental expertise, business planning, market research, finance, design, and communication. Similarly, a renewable-energy innovation may require engineering expertise alongside entrepreneurship and business-development skills. EcoHack+ therefore encourages participants from different backgrounds to collaborate. Applicants who do not yet have a team can potentially use the hackathon and networking activities to meet other participants and form multidisciplinary teams. What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying Potential applicants should consider several questions before submitting an application. Clearly Define the Problem What environmental or resource-efficiency challenge does your idea address? Explain the Proposed Solution How does your idea address the problem? Identify the Target Users Who would use or benefit from the solution? Consider Sustainability How would the solution contribute to a greener or more circular economy? Think About Feasibility Can the idea realistically be developed, tested, implemented, or scaled? Consider the Market If the solution is commercial, who would pay for it and why? Identify the Stage of Development Is your idea: An early concept? A prototype? An existing startup? An established MSME looking to adopt sustainable practices? Understanding the current stage of the project can help applicants determine which program track is most appropriate. Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program provides a structured pathway for developing innovative solutions to environmental and resource-efficiency challenges in the West Bank, including Jerusalem. By combining hackathons, technical assistance, specialized mentoring, networking, incubation, and seed funding, the program is designed to help participants move from an initial idea or existing project toward a more developed and potentially market-ready solution. The program is open to different types of innovators, including university students, young innovators, researchers, early-stage startups, entrepreneurs, and micro, small and medium enterprises. Participants can apply individually or as teams, with opportunities to form multidisciplinary teams during the hackathon. With average financial support of approximately €8,000 per selected team and incubation support of up to six months, EcoHack+ provides both financial and non-financial assistance to participants working on green and circular-economy solutions. The application period is scheduled to open in September 2026 . Since a specific closing date was not provided in the information available, interested applicants should monitor the official program announcement and application platform for the deadline and complete eligibility requirements.
